nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the block containing $a$ in the discrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the singleton $\{a\}$.
nodes.title: The block of a point in the discrete noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the block containing $a$ in the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the whole set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: The block of a point in the indiscrete noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: For $n = 0$, the discrete noncrossing partition of the empty set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has no blocks: its set of blocks is empty.
nodes.title: The discrete partition of the empty set has no blocks

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the set of blocks of the discrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is exactly the set of singletons $\{a\}$ with $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: The discrete noncrossing partition consists of the singletons

nodes.summary: For $n = 0$, the discrete and the indiscrete noncrossing partitions of the empty set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are equal.
nodes.title: Discrete and indiscrete partitions agree on the empty set

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the discrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the finest partition of this set, whose blocks are the singletons $\{a\}$ for $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$; it is noncrossing.
nodes.title: Discrete noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A noncrossing partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ equals the discrete noncrossing partition if and only if $P$, viewed as a set partition, is the finest partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the discrete noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: For $n = 0$, every noncrossing partition of the empty set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ equals the discrete noncrossing partition.
nodes.title: The only noncrossing partition of the empty set is the discrete one

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A noncrossing partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ equals the indiscrete noncrossing partition if and only if $P$, viewed as a set partition, is the coarsest partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the indiscrete noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. If for every $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the block of $P$ containing $a$ is the whole set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, then $P$ is the indiscrete noncrossing partition.
nodes.title: A partition whose blocks are all the whole set is indiscrete

nodes.summary: For $n = 0$, every noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the empty set, equals the indiscrete noncrossing partition of this set.
nodes.title: The empty set has a unique noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ with $0 < n$, the set of blocks of the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $\{\{0, \dots, n-1\}\}$: its only block is the whole set.
nodes.title: The indiscrete partition of a nonempty set has a single block

nodes.summary: For $n = 0$, the set of blocks of the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the empty set, is empty.
nodes.title: The indiscrete partition of the empty set has no blocks

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the coarsest partition of this set: its only block is the whole set when $n > 0$, and it has no blocks when $n = 0$. It is noncrossing.
nodes.title: The indiscrete noncrossing partition

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the discrete partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, whose blocks are the singletons, is noncrossing.
nodes.title: The discrete partition is noncrossing

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the indiscrete partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the coarsest partition of this set, is noncrossing.
nodes.title: The indiscrete partition is noncrossing

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
